muse-spark.profile: Free auxiliary route for bounded background research, alternative drafts, and independent low-risk summaries, only when saving paid capacity matters and nobody waits on the answer. AA first answer about 58 s, so never for anything a person waits on or that blocks other work. Prefer Sol for coding and consequential factual conclusions. AA max II 48.1, terminal 33.3%, SciCode 58.8%: respectable on static reasoning, weak with tools. Never for tool-heavy or multi-step agentic work. AA's paid API measurements do not predict this contributor-free endpoint's performance or supported effort. Free-route availability can vary.

luna.profile: First choice for strictly mechanical work: exact commands, file listings, copying, and specified formatting with deterministic verification. Use low or the lowest supported effort. A parent rating of trivial or mechanical already routes here without the classifier; you see Luna only for the remaining cases. Tasks requiring interpretation, factual synthesis, nontrivial edits, debugging, or review go to Sol instead. AA max II 38.1 and terminal 12.6%; more reasoning does not turn Luna into a strong coding agent. When it does not know, it guesses: 76.7% of its non-correct knowledge answers are wrong rather than abstained, so it never answers factual questions. Its narrow classifier role is separate from these worker limits. No current local speed claim.

sonnet.profile: Preferred Claude alternative for bounded independent review of OpenAI-authored code: high effort, never lower. Sonnet medium (II 40.8, terminal 29.8%) is unusable for review or code. Its strongest role is hard terminal implementation with executable acceptance tests at xhigh: terminal 57.1%, II 51.9, about 38 s to first answer, versus Sol xhigh 54.0% at about 178 s. Sonnet max has the best terminal score in this roster (63.6%); use it only for an explicit quality-over-latency request or documented failed attempts. Sol medium leads Sonnet high on II and terminal coding at a quarter of the cost, so Sonnet is not the ordinary implementation default. Use Opus for broad architectural ambiguity, consequential cross-system review, and all UI/UX. Shares the Claude quota that the main session uses. Claude results include default fallback; no measured review-specific superiority is claimed.

haiku.profile: Cheap Claude-family auxiliary for bulk summaries, extraction, classification, and compaction, chosen when Codex quota is high or a cheap second-family check of OpenAI output is wanted. Fastest output in the roster (about 175 tokens per second) at Luna-level API prices. Medium for mechanical bulk work; high when a sentence of judgment is needed. Never for review, implementation, or debugging: AA high II 37.8 and Terminal-Bench 4.0 21.7%, below Sol low (42.1, 30.8%), which also starts faster and costs about the same per task. Anthropic describes it as a subagent for narrow, cost-sensitive tasks. Shares the Claude quota the main session uses. The bridge serves 200K context.

sol.profile: Secondary general-purpose worker. Low for bounded lookup, extraction, and docs with source evidence. Medium for ordinary implementation, localized debugging, test writing, factual synthesis, and bounded reviews of Claude-authored code. High for interacting bugs, concurrency, subtle tests, and difficult review; xhigh for a demonstrated reasoning bottleneck or exceptional terminal work. Max is not the default. AA low/medium/high/xhigh/max terminal 30.8/48.0/51.5/54.0/56.1%; II 42.1/47.8/50.2/51.0/51.8. Medium is a large step above low. High beats Astra medium on II, terminal, and SciCode. Max costs 1.84x xhigh per AA task for 0.79 II points, with non-monotonic SciCode and hallucination results. Effort has a latency cliff: AA first answer about 8 s at medium, 65 s at high, 178 s at xhigh, 339 s at max. A bug with interacting causes (cancellation plus retries, races, state across components) is high, and its one-minute start is accepted; do not downgrade such a bug to medium to save latency. Medium is for one-cause bugs and ordinary features. Use xhigh only for background work or when the parent accepts the wait, and consider Sonnet xhigh when Claude quota is healthy and the parent is waiting. Supports low through max, not off/minimal. OpenAI documents a 1.05M context window with 922K max input; Pi's catalog entry of 272K is stale, and requests above 272K input tokens are billed at double rates. Long-context reasoning (AA-LCR 82-84%) matches Opus and exceeds Astra. Use Opus for UI/UX, broad extreme architecture, and scientific or mathematical code. Uses Codex quota, not the Claude quota of the main session.

opus.profile: Required for UI/UX design and implementation. Primary general-purpose worker. Preferred for open-ended architecture, ambiguous cross-system changes, scientific or mathematical implementation, and consequential independent review of OpenAI code. Medium for bounded design or moderate escalation; high for broad hard/extreme work; xhigh for exceptional unresolved reasoning. AA medium/high/xhigh terminal 52.5/56.6/59.6%, SciCode 59.3/60.4/65.0%, II 51.2/53.6/56.0. Its clearest measured lead is SciCode: Opus medium (59.3%) beats every Sol and Astra effort level. Opus medium modestly exceeds Sol high elsewhere, but costs about 4.2x per AA task; that is not a subscription quota ratio. Sol remains the default for ordinary code. The main session itself runs on Opus, so every Opus subagent draws down the same Claude quota the user is working with; do not spend it on work Sol does as well. Default-fallback benchmark configuration may differ from the bridge. Manual escalation of a failed Opus attempt goes to Astra as a second opinion from another family, not because Astra scores higher.

astra.profile: Reserve for a fresh OpenAI attempt after difficult Sol work fails, extreme terminal reasoning, or consequential independent review of Claude code. High for difficult review; xhigh for exceptional unresolved problems. Use Sol medium/high for bounded Claude-authored reviews instead of selecting Astra merely because the task says review or security. AA medium/high/xhigh terminal 49.5/54.0/59.6%, II 49.6/50.9/52.4. Sol high leads Astra medium on all three reported quality metrics. Astra xhigh provides a terminal gain over Sol xhigh, not a universal correctness guarantee. No benchmark here proves security or defect-detection superiority. OpenAI documents the same 1.05M context window for Astra and Sol, so context size is not a reason to choose Astra. Astra medium starts fast (about 6 s to first answer) at quality close to Sol high, a fair option for an interactive hard task when Codex quota is plentiful. API cost is 5x Sol per token, and Codex quota use is assumed to scale with it. The separate fixed manual reviewer remains Astra high. Manual escalation of a failed Astra attempt goes to Fable, the last different-family step of the chain.

fable.profile: Manual or last-resort alternative only when Sol, Sonnet, Opus, and Astra are unavailable or the task has specific evidence favoring Fable. No default workload. It is the final manual escalation step after Sol, Opus, and Astra attempts; after it, escalation only raises effort. AA max II 53.35, terminal 52.0%, SciCode 63.1%, cost $7.63 per index task. These results provide no general advantage over Opus. Its highest Omniscience accuracy in the roster (67.2%) comes with a 72.6% hallucination rate on non-correct answers: it knows the most and also guesses when it does not know, so its factual output needs checking like any other. Terminal 52.0% is below Sol max; it is not a terminal specialist. Has a separate weekly model limit in this setup. API cost is not that limit's consumption. Do not infer review or research excellence from model size.

modelData: Refreshed 2026-10-12 from primary model docs and Artificial Analysis II v4.3.2/TB4/SciCode. Sol quality scores match the September snapshot; no post-release rerun date was established. Evidence and effort tables: research/subagent-routing-2026-10-12.md. Task roles are routing judgments, not benchmark-proven specialties. API cost is not subscription quota use; first-answer latency is not subagent runtime. No current local worker-speed measurements. Classifier is Luna medium; trivial or mechanical parent ratings bypass it. Keep these roles fixed until the outcomes log (subtask-router-outcomes.jsonl) has a few weeks of data, then revise from that. Preserve the Opus UI/UX preference and the fixed Astra-high manual reviewer.
